metadata.title: GPU Procurement Advice & Production AI | SonarWave Technologies
metadata.description: GPU purchase advice informed by AI development experience. SonarWave reviews quotes, coordinates vendors, deploys inference software and helps your system evolve.

hero.title: Buy the right GPU system.
hero.description: We help you choose GPU servers and workstations for the AI you need to run. From purchase advice to inference software and ongoing improvements, we turn hardware decisions into usable AI capacity.
hero.note: Founder experience in aerospace data-center procurement and government AI procurement.

pains.title: A GPU quote is only part of the decision.
pains.description: The wrong hardware or software stack can limit the return on your investment. We connect procurement decisions to how your AI will run in practice.

items.pain: Will this quote deliver what we need?
items.impact: A GPU specification alone cannot tell you whether your models will fit or your users will get the performance they need.
items.solution: We assess vendor quotes against your workloads and can test inference on cloud GPUs before you commit to a large hardware purchase.
items.outcome: A buying decision informed by workload evidence, with remaining risks made explicit.

items.pain: Are we getting enough from our GPUs?
items.impact: A poorly matched inference engine or deployment design can leave expensive hardware underused and users waiting.
items.solution: We select and tune the software that serves your models, then measure throughput and response times against agreed workloads. Testing can start on cloud GPUs before purchase and continue on your deployed system.
items.outcome: Measured performance against your requirements, with clear next steps.

items.pain: What happens when our AI needs change?
items.impact: New models, software releases and growing demand create work after launch. Your team needs a way to assess changes and manage disruption.
items.solution: We can evaluate upgrades, adapt the deployment, plan fallback options and build your team’s operating skills.
items.outcome: A scoped improvement plan that helps your system stay useful.

faq.title: Good questions.

items.question: Do you sell hardware or advise on purchases?
items.answer: We advise on purchases. If you want help with sourcing, we can work with multiple vendors and resellers to coordinate OEM products, delivery and installation. The proposal identifies who supplies the hardware, who installs it and the associated costs.

items.question: Can we start with just a quote review?
items.answer: Yes. The GPU Purchase Review is a separate engagement. You receive a written recommendation and decide whether you want vendor coordination, deployment or ongoing help.

items.question: Can we test performance before buying hardware?
items.answer: Yes. We can scope inference tests using cloud GPUs to compare throughput, response times and running costs for agreed workloads. We agree the test environment and budget upfront. Results inform the purchase recommendation; differences in hardware and configuration still need validation on the proposed system.

items.question: We already own GPUs. Can you help?
items.answer: Yes. We can assess your hardware, models and inference software, identify compatibility or performance gaps, and scope improvements against the workloads you need to run.

items.question: Can you help after deployment?
items.answer: Yes. We can help as your models, software stack and user demand evolve, including upgrade evaluation, performance tuning, fallback planning and team training. We agree the scope, schedule and support responsibilities with you; ongoing help is separate from the purchase review.

items.question: Why involve SonarWave alongside our IT team or vendor?
items.answer: Our founder brings experience in aerospace data-center procurement, government AI procurement and GenAI product development. We apply that perspective to the connection between your business requirements, proposed hardware and inference software, working with your team and vendors through evaluation, deployment and later improvements.

items.question: How are pricing and vendor coordination handled?
items.answer: We agree the service scope, fee and schedule before work starts. Hardware, licences and cloud usage are separate. If vendor coordination is included, the proposal sets out purchasing, installation and support responsibilities and costs.

items.question: Does on-premises AI keep all our data local?
items.answer: That depends on the full setup. External APIs, telemetry, model downloads and access controls need to be reviewed. We plan the deployment around your data requirements; running a model locally does not by itself guarantee privacy or compliance.

sample.title: What a GPU Purchase Review covers.
sample.description: This is an example of the review format, not a client report or a hardware recommendation. Your review is based on your workloads, quotes and agreed scope.
sample.scenario: Example brief: a team wants a local AI assistant for internal documents and is comparing GPU server quotes.

sections.title: 1. Requirements
sections.description: Record the models, inference-engine support, user demand, response-time needs, data restrictions and budget. Identify missing information before choosing hardware.

sections.title: 2. Quote assessment
sections.description: Compare each quote with the requirements. Note GPU memory, software support, storage, networking, warranty and any assumptions the vendor needs to confirm.

sections.title: 3. Installation readiness
sections.description: Check power, cooling, rack or workstation space, network access and who owns installation and system access.

sections.title: 4. Cloud validation, if scoped
sections.description: Record the tested GPU, model, inference engine, workload and configuration, alongside throughput, response times and running costs. Explain what the results mean for sizing and which differences still need validation on the proposed system.

sections.title: 5. Recommendation & validation
sections.description: Explain the recommended direction, unresolved risks and compatibility and performance checks to complete before ordering. Define what the system must demonstrate during acceptance testing.

sample.closing: The outcome is a decision record: what to buy, why it fits, and what still needs to be checked.
